title: STEP import refuses Lobe.stp: one edge lies 0.0102 mm off its face, over the 0.01 mm cap

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
The maintainer reported this in chat on 2026-11-20, on build V0.24.0 acd5b02d. He opened `Lobe.stp` (the file is `testdata/models/Lobe.step` in his checkout; it is untracked and stays local: never copy it to GitHub) and got this refusal:

```
import refused: corrupt STEP: solidcore: import_step produced an invalid result: 1 of 1 solid item(s) refused; first #14 at read: pcurves failed on 1 of 14 faces; first: face #230: kernel pcurves: edge 2 lies 0.0102 mm off the face's surface, over the cap of 0.01 mm - re-export the model, or import an STL
```

What happens: the whole solid is refused. The gap is 0.0102 mm, 2 percent over the cap of `MAX_EDGE_GAP_MM = 0.01` mm (`crates/kernel/src/solidcore_trims.rs`, line 40). The file is a legal STEP file.

Expected: a model whose edge gap is this small imports, or the refusal says why a gap of this size is unsafe. A user file must not need a re-export for 0.0002 mm.

Why `P3`: wrong behaviour that a user finds, with a workaround (re-export, or import an STL). It is not wrong output: the refusal is the safe side.

Known facts:
- The cap was set "from data": the largest gap on the fixtures that read is 1.2e-6 mm (decision `docs/decisions/917-solidcore-step.md`). Those fixtures are few. A real exporter gives gaps that are 4 orders of magnitude larger.
- The cap exists to refuse an edge that is a visible step off its face (0.25 mm on a 1 mm part, #917). 0.0102 mm is far below that.
- The file declares its own tolerance (STEP uncertainty). The cap is a fixed number and ignores it.

Research questions (post the answers in comments; file sub-issues):
- What is the gap on the real files we hold? Measure the gap per edge on `Lobe.step`, `fig8.step`, `fillet_corner.step`, `bar_cross_holes.step` and the twisted-flank file. Report the largest value for each file.
- Should the cap follow the file (its declared uncertainty, with a floor and a ceiling), the size of the model, or the machining tolerance of the operation? Name the safe rule and the reason.
- What does the old truck reader do with a 0.0102 mm gap? (`git show 3ffe2338f` has the truck path; the recorded verdicts are in the STEP bench.)
- Can the kernel heal the gap (move the edge onto the face) instead of a refusal, with the move recorded in the import notes?

Safety (AGENTS.md "Prime Directive"):
- A looser cap can accept a model with a small step, and a toolpath on such a model can gouge by that step. Any change needs pins at the new cap and just over it, and the refusal text stays by name.
- This is under the safety floor: `effort:max`.

Done means: `Lobe.step` imports, or its refusal names a defect that is real. The rule for the cap is in `docs/decisions/` with the measured gaps of each file. Pins show a gap just under the new rule is read and a gap just over is refused.

Related: #917 (closed), #2919 (short-name units), #2780 (thread flank speed).
